questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore Spanish culture, and it was the destination in Europe that I wanted to live in the most. I was also interested in learning more Spanish and wanted to improve my skills. It is a city that many people enjoy because it combines the beach and the city, which I also loved.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I actually thought it was okay to find information. They were okay quick to answer emails, but it can be a bit tricky to figure out the websites and such.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had like a welcome session for all of the exchange students, but I didn't learn that much there, and it wasn't like a mingle, but more of a sit and listen. They talked about the Catalan culture, which was nice. Nevertheless is was okay that they had that and you got introduced to Erasmus and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They make could have introduced the school more, like the basics. Things like sports, the classroom systems, canteens and so on.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a friend who lived there on exchange the year before, so I got in contact with her landlord, and then we got a 4-person apartment in the city center. Therefor I was very lucky, but I haven't heard of any who were in big trouble finding a place to live there, but some had to pay a high rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We lived on Via Laietana, which was a very big street in the city center, and it was very nice because it was close to everything. After living there for some time I wouldn't have minded living in areas like Gracia and Eixample, which were very cool areas, and not that busy as where I lived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know because I luckily got an apartment very quickly. I recommend starting early with finding housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a day where the registration opened, and we had to sit ready to register because it was first-come, first- served basis. They had technical difficulties when we had to do it haha, so it was 40 minutes of sitting and not knowing. You had to make sure yourself that the courses and exams didn't overlap

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They send e-mails with instructions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We got alle the courses that we applied for and wanted. It didn't seem that difficult to get. There were only 1 English class per course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It isn't that important that the classes is aligning perfectly after each other, because it is quite easy to catch up if you skip sometimes to go on trips and so on - and you are probably going to skip sometimes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was so different from course to course. But almost every lecturer was very nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the academic level were as expected, but we underestimated it in the beginning, so we didn't show up that much, and then when midterms came, we were a bit surprised that it was more difficult than expected; but that is because we didn't read a lot, so I wouldn't say it is hard, but you have to keep up and stay updated, maybe that is obvious haha.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is quite different from Denmark, as the classes very smaller - around 20-30 people, but they didn't take attendance or partipication. I personally liked it with the smaller classes, but in the end we missed UCPH level and teaching a lot.

Each course had different exams and ways of teaching. In Game Theory, we had two exams (midterm and final) and three assignments that counted toward the grade. But in Industrial Organization, for example, we had two continuous evaluation tests and a final exam. It can be a bit confusing that they are different.

In the beginning, we had to choose for almost every course whether to have continuous evaluation (exams throughout the course plus a final) or just one final exam. We chose continuous for all of them, but in the end, we realized we could have just chosen the single final exam, because we had to pass that no matter what.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Macroeconomics III (366726), Game Theory for Business (363712), World Economic History (366714), Industrial Organization (363669), Public Sector Economics	(363652)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Macroeconomics III (366726) and Game Theory for Business (363712). These were my favorite courses with great lecturers. World Economic History (366714) was also very interesting, but we didn't go to a lot of classes.

I think we were a bit surprised that Industrial Organization and Public Sector Economics were a bit more demanding that we thought (not crazy). I would probably have chosen some courses I found a bit more interesting than these if I could chose over again. It was basically a repetition of Micro I and Micro II back home, but without a lot of calculations, so I must say that I have learned more about the mechanisms and theory of Micro now instead of just the calculations from the courses, so that is nice to bring back haha.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You eat a lot in restaurant because the food is so good there, which were where I spend a lot of money. You also go on a lot of trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The supermarket was pretty much the same as in Copenhagen, but restaurants, shopping and other things were cheaper. We got 3 months for 336 kr in total (T-Joven card), and then you can use all the transport you want unlimited for the time period. That was the best thing. I visited a lot of cities with just a T-joven card, because it stretched that far outside of Barcelona like Sitges, Montserrat, Vilanova I la Geltrú.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Non existing I would say haha. One of my friends tried signing up for soccer, but were unsuccessful.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Barcelona!! I rented a car and went on a Costa Brava roadtrip. Go to Montserrat and hike. Take a one-day trip to the cities around Barcelona. There are so many nice places in Spain. Some of my friend also went to Andorra and hiked, which was beautiful, but go there while it is sunny unless you have warm clothing. Take the train to Badalona if you want a more chill beach. Some also visited Madrid, Lissabon.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are so sweet, and had no unpleasant encounters. They are good at English, but they start with speaking spanish to you, so if you learn some basic saying, you can get by in spanish in the supermarkets, coffee shops and so on. I never felt unsafe, but maybe because we lived in the center with a. lot of people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No sorry. We mostly talked to other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I dont think I found anything challenging about the culture, but some things are maybe a bit more outdated than in Denmark. I think everyone was so nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I dont have any new comments.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a T-joven card. Go on a lot of trips outside of the city. Explore different areas in the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I thought I needed more warm clothes for like November-december, but it was only cold cold for like a week. Much warmer than I thought. I still went out In the day in just a sweater in December.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed spain. The weather was amazing. Good cheap coffee (the best were at uni), great food, so many cutes places.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I thought that I would meet more people from other contries.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
